subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should WebSocket upgrades gain a pre-handshake security gate, and if so must it reuse the existing gateway.controlUi origin policy without a blanket default-on Sec-Fetch-Site rejection or parallel configuration keys?
rationale: Gate placement, default strictness, and permanent configuration ownership change the Gateway security and compatibility contract; review can identify defects but cannot select that product boundary.

options.title: Canonical pre-handshake gate
options.body: Add pre-handshake enforcement that reuses the existing origin and trusted-proxy policy, treats Sec-Fetch-Site as supplemental evidence, and introduces no duplicate fallback key.

options.title: Post-handshake hardening only
options.body: Keep the current admission location and add only narrowly proven forwarded-header validation to the canonical shared path.

options.title: Explicit strict mode
options.body: Keep a separate strict mode only with opt-in defaults, complete configuration documentation, defined upgrade semantics, and real behavior proof.

recommendation.title: Canonical pre-handshake gate
recommendation.body: Add pre-handshake enforcement that reuses the existing origin and trusted-proxy policy, treats Sec-Fetch-Site as supplemental evidence, and introduces no duplicate fallback key.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the current WebSocket origin contract and is explicitly asked in the discussion to decide gate placement and flag naming.
